title: Choose SnapPilot's visual world
question: The roll assigned Site Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Site Board
options.lineage: construction site signage, survey levelling staffs, high-vis and hazard chevrons
options.thesis: The books as a site notice board: safety yellow and black, readable at arm's length in equatorial sun, every number hung on one measuring rule.
options.viewport: Phone: a full-width yellow band with today's cash and bank total in huge condensed numerals; beneath it a black chevron strip counting down to the GST deadline; then a ruled staff list of money in and out, each amount right-aligned to one vertical rule. The Snap shutter is a black disc on yellow, bottom centre, thumb reach.
options.risk: Yellow and black can read as warning rather than brand if the chevrons are overused; the discipline is one yellow field per screen, never yellow everywhere.

raised.raise: One ruling axis: every line of copy and every amount hangs off a single vertical rule, like depth on a dive profile.
Every step is recoverable: undo on every action, void instead of delete, and the state names say so.
Numerals measured against a fixed graticule: tabular figures on an 8px grid, amounts always aligned to the rule.
Fixed regions that never move: navigation swaps content, never layout, so site staff learn one board.
The logo and the components share one geometric system: the mark's shutter and rule are the same shapes the UI is built from.

options.label: Carbon Daybook
options.lineage: the contractor's ruled cash book, carbonless duplicate receipt pads, rubber stamps
options.thesis: The app is the cash book the owner already keeps, with the AI as the clerk who fills the columns.
options.viewport: Phone: a ruled page with Date, What, Paid from, and Amount columns; new entries slide in as the pink copy and settle as the white top sheet; a red PAID stamp confirms.
options.risk: This is the direction most runs in this category land on. Rendered timidly it becomes skeuomorphic paper with a blue button.

options.label: Ink & Gold (current artboards)
options.lineage: the four LedgerOS artboards published today
options.thesis: Deep ink ground, one gold accent for Snap, mint and coral for money in and out, Bricolage Grotesque display.
options.viewport: Phone: bento dashboard under a gold glow, glass tab bar with a raised gold Snap button.
options.risk: Near-black with one glowing accent is the look AI tools ship most, and a dark screen is the hardest to read on a sunlit site.
options.case: Keeps what you approved this morning; the shape round then only fills in screens.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white, one monospace face, tabular columns: the ledger as a data field with nothing to distract from the numbers.
options.viewport: Phone: white field, black hairlines, every amount in a strict column; selecting a row pulls its numbers up and fades the rest.
options.case: Holds product clarity: maximum contrast and tabular numerics read anywhere. Loses audience identification: a contractor does not see himself in a gallery data piece.
options.risk: Strobing and inversion are out; without them it can feel like a spreadsheet.

options.label: Mesophotic Dive
options.lineage: technical deep dive down a volcanic wall
options.thesis: Navigate the books by depth on one vertical axis.
options.viewport: A vertical depth profile of the month.
options.case: Diving is Maldivian, but a contractor does not identify with a dive computer, and depth is a contrived axis for a ledger.
options.kept: One ruling axis for every line of copy.
options.risk: Dark ground fails on site in sunlight.

options.label: Orizuru Sequence
options.lineage: thirty-two folds of one vermilion sheet
options.thesis: The snap flow as numbered, recoverable folds.
options.viewport: A centred square with the active step in the margin.
options.case: Numbered recoverable steps suit the review flow, but the whole app is not a sequence and vermilion paper says nothing to this audience.
options.kept: Recoverable states: undo everywhere, void not delete.

options.label: Oscilloscope Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: Cash as a phosphor trace over a ten-division graticule.
options.viewport: One screen, signals overlaid on a grid.
options.case: Contractors do not read scopes, and phosphor on black is unreadable in daylight.
options.kept: Every numeral measured against a fixed graticule.

options.label: PC-98 Field
options.thesis: Fixed regions, dithered gradients, a docked text window.
options.case: No identification for this audience, and a bitmap face cannot carry Thaana later.
options.kept: Fixed regions that never move; navigation swaps content, not layout.
options.risk: Nostalgia for a machine nobody here used.

options.label: Generative Identity
options.lineage: parametric mark that reseeds the whole brand
options.thesis: A logo that redraws itself and restyles every surface.
options.viewport: An animating mark in the nav, a parameters panel.
options.case: A finance app that changes its own identity undermines the one thing it must prove: that the books are stable.
options.kept: Logo and components drawn from one geometric system.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: White ground, near-black text, one blue accent, rounded cards, bottom tab bar: what Ramp, Revolut Business, and Expensify ship, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Balance card on top, transaction list below, floating action button for capture.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
